narratives.Overview:
## Summary

Two distinct testing rules from practitioner CLAUDE.md files are absent from directive's `coding/testing.md`.

## Rule 1: Test integrity — tests verify correctness, not define the solution

> When tests fail, investigate root cause and fix the underlying issue. Do not hard-code values, weaken assertions, or game around tests. If a test appears incorrect, report it.

Directive's testing standards cover coverage thresholds, test-first discipline, and the 'claim checks passed without running them' anti-pattern (#1006 Fail Loud). But the inverse failure mode — an agent that makes tests *pass* by gaming them rather than fixing the underlying code — is unaddressed.

This is a distinct, named anti-pattern: hard-coding expected values to satisfy a test, removing assertions to clear a failure, or restructuring code purely to satisfy test shapes rather than to be correct.

## Rule 2: Mock boundary — mocks are acceptable for external services, not for your own data layer

> Prefer integration tests over mocked unit tests for data flow and permissions. If a test passes with mocks but would fail against the real system, the test is wrong.

Directive's testing standards do not establish where mocking is appropriate vs where it hides real failure modes. The boundary: mock external services (third-party APIs, email providers, payment gateways), but not your own data access layer, internal services, or permission checks — those need integration tests against a real (test) instance.

## Source

alleneubank/claude-code CLAUDE.md (https://github.com/alleneubank/claude-code/blob/main/CLAUDE.md) — 'Test integrity' and 'Test realism' sections.

## Files affected

- `coding/testing.md` — two new named rule sections
- `tests/content/test_standards.py` or `tests/content/test_coding_rules.py` — content tests

## Related

- #1006 (Fail Loud — claims correctness without verification; this addresses gaming verification itself)
- #932 (tracer-bullet TDD — orthogonal; that is about vertical slicing, this is about test fidelity)

## Pain dispositions (Stop 1 P1–P4)

### P1 named sections missing — support
blocks-the-design

At pin `789dc5f36d54e7be705ca5d91fb7c14f264a0a0e`, `git show …:content/coding/testing.md` headings are only: Universal Requirements, Test-First Development, Coverage, Test Types, Language-Specific Details, Test Organization, Best Practices, Anti-patterns, CI/CD Integration. `git grep` over `content/` + content-contracts for `Test integrity`, `Mock boundary`, and `Test realism` is empty. Anti-pattern bullets (`⊗ assume its ok for a test to fail…`, `⊗ Mock everything…`) sit under `## Anti-patterns` and do not create the DCR-named sections. Stop 1’s `anti_game=True named_sections=False` read holds: bullet presence ≠ named-section discharge.

### P2 pack SoT vs hand-edit — support
blocks-the-design

Rendered file opens `<!-- AUTO-GENERATED by task packs:render -- DO NOT EDIT MANUALLY -->` / `Source of truth: packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json`. The full document body lives on pack rule `testing-001` (`path: coding/testing.md`, non-null `body`). A durable land that edits only `content/coding/testing.md` is wiped on the next `task packs:render`. Bound must name pack body/section write + render + drift check, and refuse hand-edit of the rendered file as the durable land.

### P3 Unit Tests mocks conjunct vs mock-boundary — support
blocks-the-design

Pack rule `testing-030` / Unit Tests line is still `! No external dependencies (use mocks/stubs)`. Anti-patterns only bans `⊗ Mock everything (integration tests needed too)`. That MUST licenses broad own-layer mocks. A Mock boundary that forbids mocking own data layer / permissions collides unless Bound rewrites the Unit Tests conjunct to external-only mocks (services/IO) and keeps own data layer / permissions on the real path. Without that rewrite agents can pick either MUST.

### P4 content-test / oracle bind — support, with sharpen
sharpens-framing

Support: Bound must pin a live content-contract assertion that the two named headings exist (with operative `!` / `⊗` body) and that anti-game guidance remains, without editing the DCR harness or weakening #3156.

Sharpen: at this pin the live surface is `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/coding_rules.test.ts` (heading helpers already used for `#1005` / `#1006` on hygiene/coding). `tests/content/test_coding_rules.py` / `test_standards.py` are not the live TS content-contract path Stop 1’s issue-name sketch may imply. Prefer binding new `TestIntegrity` / `MockBoundary` describes next to the existing Fail-Loud / Surface-Conflicts pattern via `readText("coding/testing.md")` after render — not a Python-only path, and not a DCR oracle edit.

## Prefer-A Bound sketch

Land Test integrity + Mock boundary as named `##` sections through the rules pack, reconcile the Unit Tests mocks conjunct, and lock the live content-contract surface.

1. Edit `content/packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json` rule `testing-001` `body` (SoT) to insert operative `## Test integrity` and `## Mock boundary` sections with RFC2119 `!` / `⊗` bullets that forbid gaming failing tests / weakening gates to go green, and that restrict mocks to external services while keeping own data layer and permissions real.
2. Rewrite the Unit Tests conjunct (`testing-030` text + matching body line) from blanket `No external dependencies (use mocks/stubs)` to an external-only mocks form that does not license mocking own data layer / permissions; keep Integration Tests as the real-dependency complement; leave `⊗ Mock everything` as a supporting anti-pattern, not the named section.
3. Run `task packs:render` so `content/coding/testing.md` regenerates from pack SoT; treat hand-edit of the rendered markdown as non-durable / refuse it as the land path; prove with `task packs:verify-drift` / `task verify:pack-drift` clean.
4. Extend `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/coding_rules.test.ts` (live surface) with heading-present + MUST + MUST_NOT assertions on `## Test integrity` and `## Mock boundary` in `coding/testing.md`, mirroring the `#1005`/`#1006` helpers; keep anti-game guidance covered. Do not edit DCR harness oracles; do not lower #3156 gate integrity to go green.

## Reject / out of contract

- Editing DCR harness oracles / `named_sections` detectors to green without landing the sections.
- Weakening #3156 gate integrity (clearing red by changing the gate rather than the product/process under test).
- Claiming `#1006` Fail Loud already covers test gaming: at pin, Fail Loud lives under `content/coding/coding.md` (`## Fail Loud: Completion Claims Require Outcome Verification (#1006)`) and targets outcome-blind completion claims, not named Test integrity / Mock boundary on `testing.md`, and not the Unit Tests mocks conjunct collision.

## Plain-language summary

Stop 1’s four pains hold on the pin. Prefer-A is pack-body sections + Unit Tests rewrite + packs:render + coding_rules.test.ts locks — not a hand-edit of rendered testing.md, not a DCR oracle tweak, and not “Fail Loud already did it.”

## Verdict: support, with a tighter Bound

P1 -- Support. At the pin, `content/coding/testing.md` has neither `## Test integrity` nor `## Mock boundary`. Its Anti-patterns prohibit skipping tests for deadlines and mocking everything, but do not explicitly prohibit weakening assertions or replacing an expected result with the buggy implementation's output. Named sections must carry operative rules, not merely satisfy a heading predicate. The DCR result is reported by Stop 1; I did not independently inspect or run the harness.

P2 -- Support and sharpen. The rendered file's first four lines explicitly identify the rules pack and `task packs:render`. In `content/packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json`, `rules[id=testing-001].body` holds the entire testing document, while individual entries also expose the guidance: `testing-030` contains the unit-test mocks conjunct; `testing-057` prohibits mocking everything; `testing-058` says to fix or remove flaky tests. Bound must update the body AND corresponding rule records, including new records for new normative rules. A body-only patch risks leaving contradictory sliced guidance even when the rendered document looks correct.

P3 -- Support the ambiguity; sharpen the claimed collision. The pin says "No external dependencies (use mocks/stubs)" but does not define external relative to a function, process, or ownership boundary. It does not yet contain the proposed Rule 2, so this is a collision the proposed change must prevent, not two already-present incompatible rules. Define the boundary by behavior under test: third-party service transport can be doubled; owned data access, query construction, permissions, and business decisions must actually execute when their correctness is asserted. An isolated caller test is not evidence that a substituted repository or permission layer works. Tests requiring a real local database belong in integration coverage; do not force every unit test to boot a database or let the unit label waive realism for data/permission claims.

P4 -- Support and narrow the evidence. The live `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/coding_rules.test.ts` is a Vitest suite despite its legacy `describe("test_coding_rules.py")` label. It uses `readText` and currently tests #1005, #1006, and lesson references; it has no testing-document constant or #1164 assertions. Extend this live suite instead of creating a retired Python path. The inspected inputs establish this extension point, not the absence of all other pack tests. Content tests can bind publication and wording; they cannot prove all future product tests resist gaming.

## Prefer-A Bound sketch

1. Author both named H2 sections in the testing-domain pack body. Keep rule records synchronized, retain existing anti-pattern protections, then generate `content/coding/testing.md` with `task packs:render`. No manual rendered-file edit as the durable change.
2. `## Test integrity`: require expected outcomes grounded in the accepted behavior contract; fix the defect exposed by a valid failing test. Prohibit deleting, skipping, xfail-marking, weakening assertions, or changing expected outcomes solely to obtain green. Incorrect tests may be corrected with explicit contract evidence and reviewed rationale, preserving regression coverage. Qualify the existing "fix or remove" flaky-test wording so it is not an escape hatch. Reference #3156's deliberate issue/PR + review route for actual gate changes; do not grant the executing agent permission to rewrite a failing gate.
3. `## Mock boundary`: permit doubles at external service boundaries; require real owned data-layer and permission behavior for claims about those behaviors, with hermetic fixtures/local dependencies where necessary. Rewrite `testing-030` AND its body occurrence along the lines of: "Keep unit tests independent of live external services; use mocks/stubs only at the boundaries allowed by Mock boundary." Explicitly route data/permission workflow verification to realistic integration tests. Reconcile "external state" as uncontrolled shared state, not a prohibition on controlled local fixtures.
4. Add a #1164 group in the existing TypeScript content-contract suite reading `coding/testing.md`. Check exact named headings and section-local normative bodies, including anti-gaming prohibitions, allowed external mocks, and owned data/permission coverage. Assert the old unconditional mocks conjunct is absent and the replacement points to Mock boundary. Bind the pack's testing body and corresponding records to the same requirements; check source/render agreement through the supported render path. Avoid a fixture that merely repeats the proposed text without reading the actual published surface.
5. Acceptance: demonstrate the new assertions fail on this pin, then pass after source edits and regeneration; rerender to establish stability; run the repository's relevant content/pack checks and normal quality gate during implementation. This critique does not claim those checks ran.

Reject out of contract: edits to DCR harness oracles or score predicates; lowering or bypassing #3156 protections; claiming #1006 already closes verification gaming. Counting passed/skipped tests and reporting verified outcomes does not establish that the assertions or doubles still test the promised behavior.

Evidence pin: [testing document](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/789dc5f36d54e7be705ca5d91fb7c14f264a0a0e/content/coding/testing.md), [rules pack](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/789dc5f36d54e7be705ca5d91fb7c14f264a0a0e/content/packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json), [live content-contract suite](https://github.com/deftai/directive/blob/789dc5f36d54e7be705ca5d91fb7c14f264a0a0e/packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/coding_rules.test.ts). Issue-context reads were limited to Stop 1 and panel-deposit at the supplied ceiling. No product implementation, ingest, or child dispatch.

## Pin facts the critique rests on

1. `rules-pack-0.1.json` carries **68** `domain: "testing"` rules, `testing-001`..`testing-068`. Exactly one (`testing-001`) has a non-null `body`; it is the whole file, 5,149 chars of markdown in a single JSON string. I verified `testing-001.body.trim() === <rendered testing.md minus its four banner comment lines>.trim()` → **true**.
2. `tasks/packs.yml:8-9, 41, 101` — `packs:render` regenerates "the proof coding/testing.md for rules"; `packs:verify-drift` is wired into `task check` and fails when ANY projection diverges. `pack-render.ts:302-310` registers `rules` with `body_field: "body"`, `path_pattern: /^(?:coding\/.+\.md|AGENTS\.md|main\.md)$/`; `pack-render.ts:454` skips null-body entries.
3. The pack's own `generated_from` reads `"coding/*.md + AGENTS.md + main.md (… coding bodies rendered …)"` while the rendered file's banner reads `Source of truth: packs/rules/rules-pack-0.1.json`. Both are true, at different times — `pack-migrate-rules` runs md→pack, `pack-render` runs pack→md.
4. `rules-pack.schema.json:34` — `id` is `{domain}-{NNN}`, "in-document order, 1-based, zero-padded", described as a "Stable, unique, deterministic slug".
5. Grep at pin for `named_sections` / `anti_game` across the whole tree: **zero hits**. The predicate lives only in the private evaluation harness.
6. `tests/content/test_standards.py` and `test_coding_rules.py` **do not exist** at pin. `tests/content/` holds only `snapshots/baseline.json` and `snapshots/known_failures.json`. The live surface is `packages/core/src/content-contracts/standards/coding_rules.test.ts`, which preserves the dead Python filename as its top `describe` label (line 27).
7. `standards.test.ts:358, 1583` are the only contract assertions touching `coding/testing.md`, and both are negative hygiene checks ("no deprecated user path", "no warping"). **No structural contract on testing.md exists today.**

## P1 — named sections missing: SUPPORT, with the oracle caveat sharpened

Supported on pin. The body has no `## Test integrity`, `## Mock boundary`, or `## Test realism`; headings are exactly: Universal Requirements / Test-First Development / Coverage / Test Types (+6 `###`) / Language-Specific Details / Test Organization / Best Practices / Anti-patterns / CI/CD Integration. The anti-game *content* is genuinely present and scattered — `testing-007` ⊗ "say a (todo-list|plan|phase|project) is done if relevant tests have not been written, run, and PASSED", `testing-008` ⊗ "assume its ok for a test to fail in any situation", `⊗ Commit failing tests`, `⊗ Ignore flaky tests`. That scatter is precisely why a detector can score anti_game=True and named_sections=False at the same time. Stop 1 reads this right.
